newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar slides below 118 yen in early Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar slides below 118 yen in early Tokyo.

text.p: The U.S. dollar slid below 118 yen in early Tokyo trade on Monday, sinking to a four-month low as investors sold the greenback on the growing belief that its two-year surge has turned around.

The dollar's latest drop followed weekend comments by key Japanese finance officials expressing pleasure with the yen's recent gains, and traders said the U.S. currency was likely to decline further during the day.

Asked over the weekend if a nearly six-yen rise against the dollar over the past week was excessive, Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, known as "Mr Yen" for his ability to sway currency markets, said: "No, it is not overly excessive."

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, in Fukuoka along with Sakakibara for a meeting of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), said he believed the yen's rise indicated that foreign exchange markets were finally digesting a Group of Seven (G7) statement made last month on currency stability.

Financial leaders of the G7 -- Japan, the United States, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Canada -- said in Washington last month that they would monitor exchange rates and cooperate as appropriate. They said currency values should reflect fundamentals and excess volatility was not desirable.

Currency markets appear to be selling dollars and buying yen on the belief that Tokyo's growing trade surplus will put upward pressure on the Japanese currency, while a possible shrinkage of the interest rate gap between the United States and Japan will make the greenback less attractive.
